article_manifest.title: MALI: 724 NEW RECRUITS UNDER THE FLAG AT SÉNOU AIR BASE 101, THE 2025 CONTINGENT READY TO PROTECT THE NATION
article_manifest.original_title: MALI : 724 NOUVELLES RECRUES SOUS LE DRAPEAU À LA BASE AÉRIENNE 101 DE SÉNOU, LE CONTINGENT 2025 PRÊT À PROTÉGER LA NATION
article_manifest.summary: The commitment and moral rearmament of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) has reached a new milestone. This Monday, October 19, 2026, the Training Center of the Senou Air Base 101 served as a framework for a solemn takeover marking the end of the Basic Common Training (FCB) for 724 young recruits of the 2025 contingent. A symbolic event of renewal, bravery and dedication to the Fatherland .

article_manifest.title: 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces: a popular cross-country to kick off the festivities
article_manifest.original_title: 66e anniversaire des Forces armées nationales : un cross populaire pour lancer les festivités
article_manifest.summary: The National Armed Forces organized a popular cross, under the sign of cohesion, as part of the commemorative activities of their 66th anniversary, Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou. As part of the commemoration of their 66th anniversary, the National Armed Forces (FAN) kicked off activities on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou On this occasion, a popular cross-country race was organized in the afternoon that mobilized elements of the Defense and Security Forces (FDS), paramilitary bodies and civilian populations.

article_manifest.title: 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces: the contribution of the military reserve discussed
article_manifest.original_title: 66e anniversaire des Forces armées nationales : l’apport de la réserve militaire discuté
article_manifest.summary: The Minister of State, Minister of War and Patriotic Defence, Major General Célestin Simporé, chaired the launch conference of the commemorative activities for the 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Ouagadougou. Burkina Faso's armed forces will blow out on November 1, 2026, their 66th candle . Thus, as part of the commemoration of this anniversary, several activities are on the agenda.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: Government reinstates the death penalty
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso: le gouvernement rétablit la peine de mort
article_manifest.summary: The Burkinabe government officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty in December last year. It had been abolished in 2018. “This legislative reform aims to strengthen public order, consolidate the fundamental values of the Nation and ensure the safety of people and property,” the Ministry of Justice wrote in a Facebook post "At the end of the votes, the Alp unanimously adopted the new law on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso," he said.

article_manifest.title: Death penalty in Burkina Faso: crimes covered by the new Penal Code
article_manifest.original_title: Peine de mort au Burkina Faso : les crimes visés par le nouveau Code pénal
article_manifest.summary: Eight years after abolishing it, Burkina Faso is putting the death penalty back into its legislation. The People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) unanimously adopted, on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 in Ouagadougou, a revised Penal Code that replaces that of 2018 . The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, presented the text on behalf of the government, with the stated objective of ensuring the safety of people and property.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso junta reinstates death penalty
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso junta reinstates death penalty
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso’s ruling junta has reinstated the death penalty, the justice ministry said Tuesday, following a unanimous vote by the West African country’s unelected legislature. The new penal code reintroducing capital punishment, which had been abolished in 2018, “aims to strengthen public order, consolidate the nation’s fundamental values and guarantee security for people and property”, the ministry said.

The new penal code reverses the abolition of capital punishment in 2018. Authorities say the move aims to strengthen public order, uphold national values and improve security.

article_manifest.title: Night rounds to secure IDP sites
article_manifest.original_title: Des rondes nocturnes pour sécuriser les sites des personnes déplacées
article_manifest.summary: In Gao, Macina, Bankass and Sévaré, IDPs and refugees face security challenges: theft of equipment, vandalism and lack of monitoring capacity. To protect their property and prevent incidents, some communities organize themselves into safety committees and multiply night rounds. But these local initiatives remain fragile and residents are demanding more protection .

At the head of the military regime that came to power at the end of September 2022 by a coup d 'état, Captain Ibrahim Traoré governs the country with an iron fist.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: the death penalty reinstated by the junta eight years after its abolition
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : la peine de mort rétablie par la junte huit ans après son abolition
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new Penal Code on Tuesday, October 20, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA), which has served as a parliament in the junta-run country since late 2022. The military regime, led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, had officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty in December last year .

article_manifest.title: Algeria Deploys Military to Bolster Sahel Security
article_manifest.original_title: Algeria Deploys Military to Bolster Sahel Security
article_manifest.summary: Algeria’s decision in August to deploy elements of its military to support Niger’s ruling junta was more than simply a policy shift: It showed that one of Africa’s strongest militaries is prepared to project its power in the name of maintaining stability in the Sahel, according to analysts. The day after the Aug. 29 mutiny by a group of Nigerien soldiers, Algeria dispatched four Sukhoi Su-30 fighter jets and an air-to-air refueling plane to Niger’s Air Base 101 in Niamey.

article_manifest.title: Menaka: at least 48 civilians killed in attacks on camps
article_manifest.original_title: Ménaka : au moins 48 civils tués dans des attaques contre des campements
article_manifest.summary: At least 48 civilians were reportedly killed on Sunday, October 18, in attacks on camps near Menaka in northeastern Mali. The Executive Office of the Idaksahak community accuses elements of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS). This violence occurs in the context of clashes between rival armed groups in the region.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Violence in the centre of the country - “We fled by canoe in the middle of the night”
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: Violences dans le centre du pays - « Nous avons fui en pirogue au milieu de la nuit »
article_manifest.summary: Depuis le début du mois de septembre, le centre du Mali est le théâtre d'une recrudescence des violences qui a fait des dizaines de victimes et provoqué le déplacement de milliers de personnes. Face à ce nouveau flux de déplacés, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a mis en place une clinique mobile dans la ville de Macina, où converge un grand nombre de familles.

article_manifest.title: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State attacks the Idaksahak community in the Menaka region
article_manifest.original_title: Massacre au Mali : l’État islamique s’attaque à la communauté idaksahak dans la région de Ménaka
article_manifest.summary: Massacre in Mali: Islamic State Tackles Idaksahak Community in Menaka Region The Islamic State terrorist attack claimed the lives of at least 48 civilians in the Menaka region of Mali. This massacre, targeting the Idaksahak community and perpetrated in retaliation for military operations, marks a tragic escalation. At least 48 civilians were killed by fighters of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISS) (ex-Islamic State in the Greater Sahara) on Sunday, October 18, in Tagadayat, in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men (security and local sources)
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés (sources sécuritaires et locales)
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks by armed men in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, several security, local and associative sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.

article_manifest.title: Militants Kill 50 Civilians in Mali in Retaliation for 'Azawad Movement'
article_manifest.original_title: مسلحون يقتلون 50 مدنيا في مالي انتقاما من "حركة أزواد"
article_manifest.summary: ملخص قال مصدر أمني إن المسلحين "أطلقوا النار على كل ما يتحرك، وقُتل 50 مدنياً، بينهم شباب وكبار في السن"، مشيراً إلى أن نازحين فروا من العنف بدأوا بالوصول إلى ميناكا أمس الإثنين، وتحدث مسؤول محلي عن عدد أكبر من القتلى، قائلاً إن الحصيلة "تتخطى 50 قتيلاً، بينهم نساء وكبار في السن". قُتل 50 مدنياً بهجمات شنها مسلحون نهاية الأسبوع الماضي على مخيمات في منطقة ميناكا شمال شرقي مالي، وفق ما أفادت مصادر أمنية وأخرى محلية وكالة الصحافة الفرنسية أمس الإثنين.

article_manifest.title: Macina hosts more than 3,400 displaced people after the September violence
article_manifest.original_title: Macina accueille plus de 3 400 déplacés après les violences de septembre
article_manifest.summary: RIGHT NOW More than 3,400 displaced people have reached Macina after the violence that occurred in September in several localities in the Ségou region, according to a report published on 16 October by Médecins Sans Frontières. MSF cites an attack in Souleye on September 1 and another in Touara on September 15. The identity of the authors and the complete human toll remain to be established .

article_manifest.title: More than 40 civilians killed in armed attack in northeast Mali
article_manifest.original_title: مقتل أكثر من 40 مدنيا في هجوم مسلح شمال شرقي مالي
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians have been killed in attacks by militants on camps in Mali's northeastern Menaka region, AFP quoted security and local sources as saying. The sources reported that the attackers used motorcycles to reach camps inhabited mostly by members of the Dussaq tribe, whose executive body accused the Islamic State of being behind the killings. According to the sources, the Dussac tribe is the cradle of the armed “Movement for the Salvation of Azawad”, allied with the government, in Bamako.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés
article_manifest.summary: Mali: more than forty civilians killed on Sunday by armed men More than forty civilians were killed on Sunday during attacks perpetrated by armed men in the Ménaka region, in northeastern Mali, causing population displacements, several security sources, local and associative, told AFP on Monday These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.

article_manifest.title: Kati: a prayer session in memory of the victims of the crisis
article_manifest.original_title: Kati : une séance de prières en mémoire des victimes de la crise
article_manifest.summary: The Minister of Religious Affairs, Worship and Customs, Dr. Mahamadou Koné, took part, on Sunday, October 18, 2026 in Kati, in a prayer and sacrifice session organized by the military hierarchy in memory of the civilian and military victims of the crisis in Mali . The ceremony was attended by Major General Oumar Diarra, Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence, military officials and bereaved families.

article_manifest.title: MENAKA: 48 civilians killed in Daesh attacks
article_manifest.original_title: MÉNAKA : 48 civils tués dans des attaques de Daesh
article_manifest.summary: "At least 48 civilians were killed on Sunday, October 18, 2026, in an armed attack in the locality of Tagadayat, in the region of Menaka". The information was reported yesterday, Monday, October 19, 2026, by the executive office of the Idaksahak community, which attributes this attack to armed men affiliated with the Islamic State group (Daesh). Source: The Renewal Indicator

article_manifest.title: Defence and Security: 678 young soldiers trained and presented to the flag in Koutiala
article_manifest.original_title: Défense et Sécurité : 678 jeunes soldats formés et présentés au drapeau à Koutiala
article_manifest.summary: Brigadier General Harouna Samaké, Governor of the Koutiala region, today formalized the end of the training course for 678 soldiers of contingent 2025, in a ceremony marked by the presentation to the flag. After six months of Basic Common Training (FCB), these 678 recruits – out of the 680 initially hired – have successfully completed their course .

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: Justice: Opening of the combined hearings of the correctional and criminal chambers of the Military Court of Mopti
article_manifest.original_title: Justice : Ouverture des audiences couplées des chambres correctionnelle et criminelle du Tribunal militaire de Mopti
article_manifest.summary: Mopti, October 20 (AMAP) The work of the combined hearings of the correctional chamber and the criminal chamber of the Military Court (TM) of Mopti, for the year 2026, began on Monday, October 19, 2026, at the headquarters of the said court in Sévaré, noted AMAP. Scheduled from 19 to 29 October, these hearings have 43 cases on the docket, involving 72 defendants including 69 military and 3 civilians .

article_manifest.title: Bamako: two suspects arrested in a burglary case involving more than 200 million FCFA
article_manifest.original_title: Bamako : deux suspects interpellés dans une affaire de cambriolages portant sur plus de 200 millions FCFA
article_manifest.summary: The Police Station of the Shopping Center arrested, on the night of October 14 to 15, 2026, two individuals suspected of being involved in several burglaries of shops in Bamako and its surroundings . The operation was conducted under the direction of Chief Commissioner Josué Kamaté, assisted by his deputy, Commissioner Issa Kouma. The investigation, opened following several complaints, made it possible to identify 14 businesses victims of these acts, for a declared damage of more than 200 million FCFA .

article_manifest.title: More than 40 civilians killed in Mali attack blamed on Islamic State
article_manifest.original_title: More than 40 civilians killed in Mali attack blamed on Islamic State
article_manifest.summary: Security and community sources in Mali says more than 40 civilians were killed over the weekend in an attack by armed men on camps in the north-eastern Menaka region. They reportedly arrived on motorcycles and targeted camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community. The community's executive bureau has blamed the killings on the Islamic State group.

article_manifest.title: Uganda: Rwandan opponent in exile, Robert Kabera, found dead
article_manifest.original_title: Ouganda: l’opposant rwandais en exil, Robert Kabera, a été retrouvé mort
article_manifest.summary: Robert Kabera, 50, a Rwandan refugee in Uganda and a former non-commissioned officer in the Rwandan army who became an ardent critic of the government of Paul Kagame was found beheaded near the capital Kampala. The announcement was made on Monday, October 19, 2026 by the Ugandan police. Robert Kabera had fled his country Rwanda in November 2020 after he was accused of sexual assault, which he has always denied .

article_manifest.title: Menaka: Idaksahak community reports 48 civilians killed in Tagadayat
article_manifest.original_title: Ménaka : la communauté Idaksahak fait état de 48 civils tués à Tagadayat
article_manifest.summary: Menaka: the Idaksahak community reports 48 civilians killed in Tagadayat The Idaksahak community reports the death of 48 civilians in an attack attributed to Daesh elements on Sunday, October 18, 2026, in the locality of Tagadayat, in the Menaka region. Injuries are also reported, according to a statement from its executive office issued on October 19 According to this organization, the attackers arrived on motorcycles and the violence caused many families to flee.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : plus d’une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés

article_manifest.title: Mali. Human Rights Watch denounces war crimes on both sides

article_manifest.summary: Burkina/Justice: The death penalty reintroduced into the Penal Code, sanctions revised upwards The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, defended, this Tuesday, October 20, 2026 before the parliamentarians of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp), the bill revising Law No. 025-2018/AN of May 25, 2018 on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso At the end of the votes, the Alp unanimously adopted the new law on the Penal Code in Burkina Faso, with the reintroduction of the death penalty (which had been abolished on 31 May 2018).

article_manifest.summary: Aerial view of the city of Menaka, November 22, 2020 in Mali At least 48 civilians were killed on Sunday during attacks perpetrated by jihadists in the Menaka region, in northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, according to a new report communicated Tuesday to AFP by concordant sources Since 2012, Mali has been plagued by a deep security crisis fuelled by violence from groups affiliated with Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State (IS) organization, as well as community-based criminal groups and Tuareg independence movements.
